centralQuestion: How did natural nuclear reactors operate about two billion years ago without anyone building them?
thesis: Ancient fuel composition, concentrated ore, neutron economy and groundwater moderation enabled natural nuclear chain reactions.
viewerPayoff: Understand how evidence exposed natural fission and how ancient fuel, concentrated ore, groundwater and surviving neutrons sustained it.

sources.organization: Comptes Rendus Geoscience / Bentridi et al.
sources.title: Inception and evolution of Oklo natural nuclear reactors (2011)
sources.notes: Full relevant article text inspected; no raw neutron-transport simulation reproduced. Model concerns specific zones and reconstructed conditions; no universal concentration, dimensions or water threshold.

sources.title: Oklo Reactors and Implications for Nuclear Science (2014)
sources.notes: Relevant pages inspected in parsed PDF; review synthesizes original investigations, not independent raw-data replication. Approximate age, inferred activity. RZ13 pulse estimates must not be generalized to all reaction zones.

sources.title: The Workings of an Ancient Nuclear Reactor (original October 2005; web 2009)
sources.notes: Author explanatory account inspected; popular participant exposition, not a second independent experiment. sources.title: DOE/EIS-0288D (1998), Appendix A: Nuclear Fission Reactors
sources.notes: Only relevant Appendix A body inspected, not entire environmental impact statement. Basic scattering mechanism only; modern engineered control-rod descriptions not imported into Oklo.

claims.statement: Groundwater served as a neutron moderator: collisions, especially with hydrogen, slowed neutrons, increasing the likelihood of further U235 fission.

evidence.locator: Sections 1–3: geological context, initial criticality conditions, numerical modeling; conclusions
evidence.notes: Water is a moderator, not fuel or a chemical trigger. Slowing is distinct from neutron absorption. Hydrogen specificity follows basic elastic-scattering physics, compatible with water moderation.
